title: Machine-learning Treg framework identifies SMARCC1 as a previously unrecognized regulator
summary: A framework combining single-cell ATAC-seq, motif analysis, topic modeling, machine learning and genetic variation identified SMARCC1 as a previously unrecognized controller of regulatory T-cell chromatin programs. CRISPR-Cas9 deletion of Smarcc1 in Tregs produced the predicted loss of accessibility in topic-3 regulatory regions, supporting the computationally inferred connection.
ai_technology: Integrated machine-learning framework using topic modeling and high-density genetic variation over single-cell ATAC-seq profiles
organization: Harvard Medical School and Imagine Institute, University of Paris

evidence.tested: A framework combining single-cell ATAC-seq, motif analysis, topic modeling, machine learning and genetic variation identified SMARCC1 as a previously unrecognized controller of regulatory T-cell chromatin programs.
evidence.unknown: CRISPR validation supported the predicted SMARCC1 effect for topic 3; topic 10 was not represented and the authors note possible redundancy with SMARCC2. The result concerns regulatory chromatin programs in Tregs, not clinical or therapeutic outcomes.
evidence.ai_role: The framework organized co-varying open chromatin regions into Treg regulatory modules, inferred transcription-factor effects on those programs, and nominated SMARCC1 as a regulator of topic-3/10 accessibility. The team tested the prediction by CRISPR-Cas9 editing Tregs and profiling chromatin accessibility.
